violation_type.title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §747.303(a)(2))
violation_type.short_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization
violation_type.typical_finding: Based on the evidence obtained during the investigation, a child was injured while in care and had to seek medical treatment. The operation failed to notify Child Care Regulation within the two-day timeframe of this occurring.

finding_variants.text: Based on the evidence obtained during the investigation, a child was injured while in care and had to seek medical treatment. The operation failed to notify Child Care Regulation within the two-day timeframe of this occurring.

Based on the information gathered during the investigation, there's sufficient evidence the Primary Caregiver did not contact CCR within 48hrs. after finding out a child was seen by a medical professional and required medical treatment.
Evidence gathered during this investigation shows a child in care was injured and received medical attention.  Licensing was not notified of the incident.
It was determined that a child broke their arm while in care in August of 2024 and this was not reported to Child Care Regulations.
The operation did not report an incident in which a child was injured and received medical attention.
This standard was evaluated and found deficient.    The caregiver did not self-report an incident where child was injured and needed medical attention.
